meet.title: At a language school
meet.text:
Anna: Hello! I'm Anna. What's your name?
Kenji: Hi, Anna. My name's Kenji.
Anna: Nice to meet you, Kenji.
Kenji: Nice to meet you too. Where are you from?
Anna: I'm from Russia. I'm from Kazan. And you?
Kenji: I'm from Japan. I'm from Osaka, but I'm in London now.
Anna: Are you a student here?
Kenji: Yes, I am. Are you a student too?
Anna: No, I'm not. I'm a teacher. I'm your Russian teacher!
Kenji: Oh! Sorry! Good morning, teacher.
Anna: That's OK, Kenji. Please call me Anna.

tr.en: Summary: Anna (from Kazan, Russia) and Kenji (from Osaka, Japan) meet at a school in London. Kenji is a student. Anna is not a student — she is his Russian teacher.

lessons.subtitle: Hello! Good morning. Bye!

text.en: **Hello** is for everybody. **Hi** is for friends. *Hello, Mr Smith.* · *Hi, Tom!*
text.ru: **Hello** подходит для всех. **Hi** — для друзей и знакомых. *Hello, Mr Smith.* · *Hi, Tom!*

text.en: **Good morning** — before 12:00. **Good afternoon** — 12:00 to 18:00. **Good evening** — after 18:00. **Good night** is NOT a greeting: you say it when you go to bed or go home late.
text.ru: **Good morning** — до 12:00. **Good afternoon** — с 12:00 до 18:00. **Good evening** — после 18:00. **Good night** — НЕ приветствие: так говорят, когда идут спать или уходят поздно вечером.

text.en: **Goodbye** — for everybody. **Bye** and **See you** — for friends. **See you later** = we meet again today or soon.
text.ru: **Goodbye** — для всех. **Bye** и **See you** — для друзей. **See you later** — увидимся сегодня или скоро.

text.en: **Please** — when you ask: *A coffee, please.* **Thank you / Thanks** — when you get something. The answer is **You're welcome.** **Sorry** — after a mistake. **Excuse me** — before a question to a person you don't know: *Excuse me, are you Mr Smith?*
text.ru: **Please** — когда просите: *A coffee, please.* **Thank you / Thanks** — когда что-то получили. Ответ — **You're welcome.** **Sorry** — после ошибки. **Excuse me** — перед вопросом к незнакомому человеку: *Excuse me, are you Mr Smith?* Русское «пожалуйста» — это два разных слова: **please** (просьба) и **you're welcome** (ответ на спасибо).

lessons.subtitle: I'm Anna. Are you Tom? — Yes, I am.

text.en: English always has a verb. With names, jobs, countries and adjectives the verb is **be**: *I **am** Anna.* *You **are** a student.*
text.ru: В английском предложении всегда есть глагол. С именами, профессиями, странами и прилагательными это глагол **be**: *I **am** Anna.* *You **are** a student.* По-русски мы говорим «Я Анна», «Ты студент» без глагола, а по-английски так нельзя: *~~I Anna~~* → *I **am** Anna.*

text.en: In speaking we use short forms: **I'm** = I am, **you're** = you are, **my name's** = my name is, **what's** = what is.
text.ru: В речи используют краткие формы: **I'm** = I am, **you're** = you are, **my name's** = my name is, **what's** = what is.

text.en: *You are a student.* → ***Are you** a student?* Short answers: **Yes, I am.** (not ~~Yes, I'm~~) · **No, I'm not.**
text.ru: *You are a student.* → ***Are you** a student?* Краткие ответы: **Yes, I am.** (не ~~Yes, I'm~~) · **No, I'm not.**

text.en: Jobs need **a** (or **an** before a, e, i, o, u): *I'm **a** teacher.* *You're **a** student.* *I'm **an** engineer.*
text.ru: Перед профессией нужен артикль **a** (или **an** перед a, e, i, o, u): *I'm **a** teacher.* *You're **a** student.* *I'm **an** engineer.* В русском артиклей нет, поэтому про них легко забыть.

text.en: ***What's your name?*** — *My name's Anna.* / *I'm Anna.* · ***Nice to meet you.*** — *Nice to meet you **too**.* · ***How are you?*** — *I'm fine, thanks. **And you?*** · ***This is** my friend Tom.*
text.ru: ***What's your name?*** — *My name's Anna.* / *I'm Anna.* · ***Nice to meet you.*** — *Nice to meet you **too**.* · ***How are you?*** — *I'm fine, thanks. **And you?*** · ***This is** my friend Tom.* На *How are you?* отвечают коротко и позитивно — это часть приветствия, а не вопрос о здоровье.

lessons.subtitle: How do you spell that? A-N-N-A.

text.en: The English alphabet has 26 letters. Learn the **names** of the letters — you need them to spell your name and e-mail address.
text.ru: В английском алфавите 26 букв. Выучите **названия** букв — они нужны, чтобы продиктовать имя или адрес электронной почты.

table: B · C · D · E · G · P · T · V
F · L · M · N · S · X · Z (zed)

text.en: **A** /eɪ/ · **E** /iː/ · **I** /aɪ/ — easy to mix up. **G** /dʒiː/ and **J** /dʒeɪ/. **W** = “double-u”. **Z** = “zed” in British English (“zee” in American English). Two same letters: **NN** = “double n”.
text.ru: **A** /eɪ/ · **E** /iː/ · **I** /aɪ/ легко перепутать: английская **E** звучит как русское «и», а **I** — как «ай». **G** /dʒiː/ и **J** /dʒeɪ/. **W** = «double-u». **Z** = «zed» в британском английском («zee» в американском). Две одинаковые буквы: **NN** = «double n».

text.en: ***How do you spell that?*** / ***How do you spell** your surname?* — *L-O-P-E-Z.* · ***Can you repeat that, please?*** · ***Can you say that again, slowly?*** · ***Sorry, I don't understand.***
text.ru: ***How do you spell that?*** / ***How do you spell** your surname?* — *L-O-P-E-Z.* · ***Can you repeat that, please?*** · ***Can you say that again, slowly?*** · ***Sorry, I don't understand.*** Пока запомните эти фразы целиком — грамматику *do* и *can* разберём позже.

text.en: *Maria Lopez*: **first name** = Maria, **surname** (or *last name*, *family name*) = Lopez. In English the first name comes first.
text.ru: *Maria Lopez*: **first name** — Maria, **surname** (или *last name*, *family name*) — Lopez. В английском сначала идёт имя, потом фамилия. Отчества нет.

text.en: 0 zero · 1 one · 2 two · 3 three · 4 four · 5 five · 6 six · 7 seven · 8 eight · 9 nine · 10 ten · 11 eleven · 12 twelve
text.ru: 0 zero · 1 one · 2 two · 3 three · 4 four · 5 five · 6 six · 7 seven · 8 eight · 9 nine · 10 ten · 11 eleven · 12 twelve

text.en: 13 thir**teen** · 14 four**teen** · 15 fif**teen** · 16 six**teen** · 17 seven**teen** · 18 eigh**teen** · 19 nine**teen** · 20 twenty. Look at the spelling: **thir**teen (not ~~threeteen~~), **fif**teen (not ~~fiveteen~~), eigh**t**een (one t).
text.ru: 13 thir**teen** · 14 four**teen** · 15 fif**teen** · 16 six**teen** · 17 seven**teen** · 18 eigh**teen** · 19 nine**teen** · 20 twenty. Обратите внимание на написание: **thir**teen (не ~~threeteen~~), **fif**teen (не ~~fiveteen~~), eigh**t**een (одна t).

text.en: ***How old are you?*** — *I**'m** twenty.* / *I**'m** twenty **years old**.* English uses **be** for age: *I **am** 20*, not ~~I have 20 years~~.
text.ru: ***How old are you?*** — *I**'m** twenty.* / *I**'m** twenty **years old**.* Возраст в английском — с глаголом **be**: *I **am** 20* (буквально «я есть двадцать»), а не ~~I have 20 years~~ и не ~~to me 20~~.

text.en: Say every number one by one: *07700 900152* = “oh seven seven oh oh, nine oh oh, one five two”. **0** in a phone number is **oh** (or zero). **77** = “double seven”. ***What's your phone number?***
text.ru: Номер читают по одной цифре: *07700 900152* = «oh seven seven oh oh, nine oh oh, one five two». **0** в номере телефона — **oh** (или zero). **77** = «double seven». ***What's your phone number?***

lessons.subtitle: I'm from Russia. I'm in London. I'm at home.

text.en: ***Where are you from?*** — *I'm **from** Russia.* / *I'm **from** Kazan.* Look: in the question, **from** is at the end.
text.ru: ***Where are you from?*** — *I'm **from** Russia.* / *I'm **from** Kazan.* Обратите внимание: в вопросе **from** стоит в конце — «Где вы из?».

h.en: in — inside a country or city

text.en: *I'm **in** London now.* *Kazan is **in** Russia.* Use **in** for countries, cities, rooms: *in Spain, in Paris, in the classroom*.
text.ru: *I'm **in** London now.* *Kazan is **in** Russia.* **in** — для стран, городов, помещений: *in Spain, in Paris, in the classroom*.

h.en: at — a point: home, work, school

text.en: *I'm **at** home.* *I'm **at** work.* *I'm **at** school.* No article here. Compare: *I'm **in** London, **at** work.* (city → **in**, place of activity → **at**)
text.ru: *I'm **at** home.* *I'm **at** work.* *I'm **at** school.* Без артикля. Сравните: *I'm **in** London, **at** work.* (город → **in**, место занятия → **at**). По-русски везде «в» или «на», а в английском это два разных предлога — запоминайте их вместе с существительным.

text.en: *I'm from **Spain**.* = *I'm **Spanish**.* Countries and nationalities always have a **capital letter**: *Russia, Russian, English*. Two countries have **the**: **the** UK, **the** USA.
text.ru: *I'm from **Spain**.* = *I'm **Spanish**.* Страны, национальности и языки всегда пишутся с **большой буквы**: *Russia, Russian, English*. Две страны — с **the**: **the** UK, **the** USA.

text.en: *I **speak** Russian and **a little** English.* ***Do you speak English?*** — *Yes, a little.*
text.ru: *I **speak** Russian and **a little** English.* ***Do you speak English?*** — *Yes, a little.* Название языка обычно совпадает с национальностью: *Russian, Spanish, Chinese*.

family.title: My family
family.text:
Hi! I'm Emma and this is a photo of my family. We're from Leeds, in the UK. There are five people in the photo.

This is my mum. Her name's Sarah. She's forty-eight and she's a nurse. She's very kind, but she's always tired. This is my dad, Mark. He's fifty and he's a bus driver. He's tall and very funny.

I've got one brother and one sister. My brother's name is Jack. He's sixteen and he's at school. He's really clever. My sister's name is Lily. She's only seven. She's small and very happy.

We've got a dog too. Its name is Biscuit. It's old, but it's very friendly. We haven't got a cat.

And this is me! I'm twenty-two. I'm not married, but I've got a boyfriend. His name's Dan. He isn't in the photo — he's at work.

tr.en: Summary: Emma (22) shows a photo of her family from Leeds: her mum Sarah (48, a nurse), her dad Mark (50, a bus driver), her brother Jack (16), her sister Lily (7) and their old dog Biscuit. Emma has a boyfriend, Dan. He is not in the photo.
tr.ru:
Привет! Я Эмма, а это фотография моей семьи. Мы из Лидса, Великобритания. На фото пять человек.

Ещё у нас есть собака. Её зовут Бисквит. Она старая, но очень дружелюбная. Кошки у нас нет.

А это я! Мне двадцать два. Я не замужем, но у меня есть парень. Его зовут Дэн. Его нет на фото — он на работе.

party.title: At a party
party.text:
Tom: Hi, Maria! Nice party!
Maria: Hi, Tom! Thanks. Who's that man with your sister?
Tom: That's Ben. He's her husband.
Maria: Oh, is she married? Is he a doctor too?
Tom: No, he isn't. He's an engineer. They've got two children.
Maria: Really? How old are they?
Tom: Their son is four and their daughter is only a baby.
Maria: Are they here?
Tom: No, they aren't. They're at home with my parents.
Maria: And you, Tom? Have you got any children?
Tom: No, I haven't. I'm single. But I've got a cat!
Maria: What's its name?
Tom: Her name's Luna. She's very beautiful.

tr.en: Summary: At a party Maria asks Tom about the man with his sister. It is Ben, her husband, an engineer. They have a son (4) and a baby daughter; the children are at home with Tom's parents. Tom is single and has a cat, Luna.

text.en: **I** am · **he / she / it** is · **you / we / they** are. Short forms: *I'm, he's, she's, it's, you're, we're, they're*.
text.ru: **I** am · **he / she / it** is · **you / we / they** are. Краткие формы: *I'm, he's, she's, it's, you're, we're, they're*. По-русски глагола нет («Она врач»), а в английском он обязателен: *She **is** a doctor.*

text.en: **he** — a man or boy · **she** — a woman or girl · **it** — a thing, an idea, often an animal. *This is my phone. **It**'s new.*
text.ru: **he** — мужчина или мальчик · **she** — женщина или девочка · **it** — предмет, понятие, часто животное. *This is my phone. **It**'s new.* У предметов в английском нет рода: «книга — она» по-английски всё равно **it**.

text.en: Add **not**: *He **isn't** a teacher.* (= He's not) · *They **aren't** at home.* (= They're not) · *I**'m not** tired.*
text.ru: Добавляем **not**: *He **isn't** a teacher.* (= He's not) · *They **aren't** at home.* (= They're not) · *I**'m not** tired.*

text.en: ***Is she** a doctor?* — *Yes, she **is**.* / *No, she **isn't**.* · ***Are they** here?* — *Yes, they **are**.* / *No, they **aren't**.* With question words: ***Who is** he?* ***Where are** they?* ***How old is** she?*
text.ru: ***Is she** a doctor?* — *Yes, she **is**.* / *No, she **isn't**.* · ***Are they** here?* — *Yes, they **are**.* / *No, they **aren't**.* С вопросительными словами: ***Who is** he?* ***Where are** they?* ***How old is** she?* В кратком ответе «да» краткую форму не используют: ~~Yes, she's.~~

text.en: Some plurals are irregular: one **man** → two **men** · one **woman** → two **women** /ˈwɪmɪn/ · one **child** → two **children** · one **person** → two **people**.

text.en: **its** = of it: *The dog is in **its** bed.* · **it's** = it is: ***It's** a dog.*

flat.title: My new flat
flat.text:
Hi Mum!

I'm in my new flat in Manchester. It's small, but it's really nice. There are three rooms: a living room, a bedroom and a kitchen. There's a bathroom too, of course, with a shower. There isn't a bath.

The living room is my favourite room. There's a big blue sofa and there are two chairs. The TV is opposite the sofa. There's a table next to the window, and my laptop is on the table. There are some shelves above the table, but there aren't any books on them — the books are still in boxes under my bed!

In the bedroom there's a bed, a wardrobe and a small desk. There's a mirror on the wall between the wardrobe and the door.

The kitchen is very small. There's a fridge and a cooker, but there isn't a table. There's a balcony, and there are some plants on it. There isn't a garden.

Are there any shops near the flat? Yes, there are! There's a supermarket opposite the house.

Love,
Emma

tr.en: Summary: Emma writes to her mum about her new small flat in Manchester: a living room (blue sofa, two chairs, TV opposite the sofa, table next to the window, empty shelves), a bedroom (bed, wardrobe, desk, mirror), a very small kitchen with no table, a bathroom with a shower, and a balcony with plants. Her books are in boxes under the bed. There is a supermarket opposite the house.
tr.ru:
Привет, мам!

Я в своей новой квартире в Манчестере. Она маленькая, но очень приятная. Здесь три комнаты: гостиная, спальня и кухня. Ванная, конечно, тоже есть — с душем. Ванны нет.

Гостиная — моя любимая комната. Там большой синий диван и два стула. Телевизор стоит напротив дивана. Рядом с окном стол, а на столе мой ноутбук. Над столом несколько полок, но книг на них нет — книги до сих пор в коробках под кроватью!

В спальне кровать, шкаф и маленький письменный стол. На стене между шкафом и дверью висит зеркало.

Кухня очень маленькая. Есть холодильник и плита, но стола нет. Есть балкон, на нём несколько растений. Сада нет.

Есть ли рядом с квартирой магазины? Да, есть! Напротив дома супермаркет.

Целую,
Эмма

lost.title: Where are my keys?
lost.text:
Dan: Emma, where are my keys?
Emma: Are they in your bag?
Dan: No, they aren't. And they aren't in my coat.
Emma: Look on the table in the hall.
Dan: There are some keys here, but these are your keys, not mine.
Emma: What about that box next to the door?
Dan: No. There's only an old umbrella in it.
Emma: Is that your wallet under the chair?
Dan: Oh yes, it is! Thanks! But where are the keys?
Emma: Dan… what's that in your hand?
Dan: This? It's my phone and… oh. My keys.
Emma: You're really tired today!

tr.en: Summary: Dan is looking for his keys. They are not in his bag, his coat, on the hall table or in the box next to the door. Emma finds his wallet under the chair. In the end the keys are in Dan's hand, with his phone.

text.en: Use **a / an** with one thing when it is new or not special: *It's **a** pen.* *I've got **an** umbrella.* **a** + consonant sound, **an** + vowel sound: *a book, a key* · *an apple, an umbrella, an old book*.
text.ru: **a / an** ставят перед одним предметом, когда он новый для собеседника или «один из многих»: *It's **a** pen.* *I've got **an** umbrella.* **a** — перед согласным звуком, **an** — перед гласным: *a book, a key* · *an apple, an umbrella, an old book*.

text.en: Use **the** when you and the listener know which thing: *Where's **the** key?* (the key to our flat) · *I've got a dog and a cat. **The** dog is old.* (second time)

Подсказка: если по-русски можно добавить «этот самый» — нужен **the**; если «какой-то, один» — **a / an**.

text.en: A countable noun in the singular is never alone: ***a** bag, **the** bag, **my** bag, **this** bag* — not ~~It's bag~~.

lessons.subtitle: There's a sofa. There aren't any chairs.

title.en: Saying what exists in a place

h.en: there is + one, there are + two or more
h.ru: there is + один, there are + два и больше

text.en: ***There's** a sofa in the living room.* (one) · ***There are** two chairs.* (two or more). We use it to say something exists **for the first time**.
text.ru: ***There's** a sofa in the living room.* (один) · ***There are** two chairs.* (два и больше). Так сообщают о предмете **впервые**. По-русски мы начинаем с места: «В гостиной (есть) диван», а по-английски — с **there is**, место ставится в конец.

text.en: *There **isn't** a bath.* · *There **aren't any** books.* · ***Is there** a garden?* — *Yes, there **is**.* / *No, there **isn't**.* · ***Are there any** shops?* — *Yes, there **are**.* / *No, there **aren't**.*
text.ru: *There **isn't** a bath.* · *There **aren't any** books.* · ***Is there** a garden?* — *Yes, there **is**.* / *No, there **isn't**.* · ***Are there any** shops?* — *Yes, there **are**.* / *No, there **aren't**.*

text.en: With plurals: **some** in positive sentences (*There are **some** plants.*), **any** in negatives and questions (*There aren't **any** plants.* *Are there **any** plants?*). **lots of** = a large number: *There are **lots of** books.*
text.ru: Со множественным числом: **some** в утвердительных предложениях (*There are **some** plants.*), **any** в отрицаниях и вопросах (*There aren't **any** plants.* *Are there **any** plants?*). **lots of** — много: *There are **lots of** books.*

text.en: **There is** introduces something new. **It is** talks about a thing we already know: ***There's** a sofa in my room. **It's** blue.* · ***There are** two chairs. **They're** old.*
text.ru: **There is** вводит новый предмет. **It is** говорит о том, что уже известно: ***There's** a sofa in my room. **It's** blue.* · ***There are** two chairs. **They're** old.* Русскоязычные часто говорят ~~It is a sofa in my room~~ — это ошибка.

text.en: ***How many** rooms **are there**?* — *There are three.* / *There's **only** one.*
text.ru: ***How many** rooms **are there**?* — *There are three.* / *There's **only** one.*

text.en: **in** — inside: *in the bag, in the box, in the kitchen* · **on** — touching the top or a wall: *on the table, on the floor, on the wall* · **under** — below: *under the bed*.
text.ru: **in** — внутри: *in the bag, in the box, in the kitchen* · **on** — на поверхности или на стене: *on the table, on the floor, on the wall* · **under** — под: *under the bed*.

text.en: **next to** — at the side of: *The lamp is **next to** the bed.* · **between** A **and** B: *The mirror is **between** the door **and** the window.* · **near** — not far: *The shop is **near** my house.*
text.ru: **next to** — рядом, вплотную: *The lamp is **next to** the bed.* · **between** A **and** B: *The mirror is **between** the door **and** the window.* · **near** — недалеко: *The shop is **near** my house.* После *near* предлог не нужен: ~~near to~~, ~~near from~~.

day.title: A day in my life
day.text:
My name's Sarah and I'm a nurse. I work at a hospital in Leeds. My day starts very early!

I get up at half past five. I have a shower, get dressed and have breakfast. I usually have coffee and toast. I never eat a big breakfast. I leave home at quarter past six and I take the bus to work. I don't drive because I haven't got a car.

I start work at seven o'clock. I work from seven to three. We don't have a long lunch break: I have lunch at about twelve, and I usually eat in the hospital café. In the afternoon I'm always tired.

I finish work at three o'clock and I go home. My daughter Lily finishes school at half past three, so I'm at home before her. In the evening I cook dinner and we eat at six. After dinner Lily does her homework and I do the housework. Then I sometimes watch TV with my husband, but I often go to bed at nine!

I don't work on Saturdays and Sundays. At the weekend I get up late, at eight o'clock.

tr.en: Summary: Sarah is a nurse in Leeds. She gets up at 5:30, leaves home at 6:15 and takes the bus. She works from 7:00 to 3:00 and has lunch at about 12:00 in the hospital café. She gets home before her daughter Lily (school finishes at 3:30). They have dinner at 6:00. Sarah often goes to bed at 9:00. She doesn't work at the weekend and gets up at 8:00.
tr.ru:
Меня зовут Сара, я медсестра. Я работаю в больнице в Лидсе. Мой день начинается очень рано!

Я встаю в половине шестого. Принимаю душ, одеваюсь и завтракаю. Обычно пью кофе с тостом. Плотно я никогда не завтракаю. Выхожу из дома в четверть седьмого и еду на работу на автобусе. Машину я не вожу, потому что у меня её нет.

Работу я начинаю в семь часов. Работаю с семи до трёх. Длинного обеденного перерыва у нас нет: я обедаю около двенадцати, обычно в кафе при больнице. Днём я всегда уставшая.

Заканчиваю в три и иду домой. Моя дочь Лили заканчивает школу в половине четвёртого, так что я дома раньше неё. Вечером я готовлю ужин, и мы едим в шесть. После ужина Лили делает уроки, а я — домашние дела. Потом я иногда смотрю телевизор с мужем, но часто ложусь спать в девять!

По субботам и воскресеньям я не работаю. В выходные встаю поздно — в восемь.

week.title: Different lives
week.text:
Jack: Mum says you study in the evening, Emma. Is that true?
Emma: Yes, it is. I work in an office from nine to five, and then I go to university on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
Jack: What time do you get home?
Emma: At about ten. I'm always tired on Wednesday mornings!
Jack: Do you study at the weekend too?
Emma: I usually study on Sunday afternoons. On Saturdays I never study. I go to the gym in the morning and I meet friends in the evening.
Jack: Does Dan go to the gym with you?
Emma: No, he doesn't. He hates the gym! He plays football twice a week. What about you? What do you do after school?
Jack: I do my homework first. Then I play computer games.
Emma: Every day?
Jack: No! Mum doesn't like it. Only on Fridays and at the weekend.

tr.en: Summary: Emma works in an office from 9 to 5 and goes to university on Tuesday and Thursday evenings; she gets home at about 10. She studies on Sunday afternoons, never on Saturdays — then she goes to the gym and meets friends. Dan hates the gym and plays football twice a week. Jack does his homework first and plays computer games only on Fridays and at the weekend.
tr.ru:
Джек: Мама говорит, ты учишься по вечерам, Эмма. Это правда?
Эмма: Да. Я работаю в офисе с девяти до пяти, а потом по вторникам и четвергам хожу в университет.
Джек: Во сколько ты приходишь домой?
Эмма: Около десяти. По средам утром я всегда уставшая!
Джек: В выходные ты тоже учишься?
Эмма: Обычно я занимаюсь в воскресенье днём. По субботам никогда. Утром хожу в спортзал, а вечером встречаюсь с друзьями.
Джек: Дэн ходит с тобой в зал?
Эмма: Нет. Он ненавидит спортзал! Он играет в футбол два раза в неделю. А ты? Что ты делаешь после школы?
Джек: Сначала делаю уроки. Потом играю в компьютерные игры.
Эмма: Каждый день?
Джек: Нет! Маме это не нравится. Только по пятницам и в выходные.

text.en: Use the **present simple** for habits and facts. With **I / you / we / they** the verb has no ending: *I **get up** at seven.* *We **live** in Leeds.* *They **work** in a hospital.*
text.ru: **Present simple** — для привычек и фактов. С **I / you / we / they** глагол без окончания: *I **get up** at seven.* *We **live** in Leeds.* *They **work** in a hospital.* Глагол *be* здесь не нужен: ~~I am get up~~, ~~I am work~~ — частая ошибка.

text.en: English uses **have** for meals and washing: ***have** breakfast / lunch / dinner* · ***have** a shower* · ***have** a coffee*. No article with meals: *I have **breakfast** at seven.* (not ~~a breakfast~~)
text.ru: С едой и мытьём — глагол **have**: ***have** breakfast / lunch / dinner* · ***have** a shower* · ***have** a coffee*. С названиями приёмов пищи артикля нет: *I have **breakfast** at seven.* (не ~~a breakfast~~). Русские «завтракать, обедать, ужинать» — это *have breakfast, have lunch, have dinner*.

text.en: ***go to** work* · ***go to** school* · ***go to** bed* — no article. But ***go home*** — no **to**! *I go home at five.* (not ~~go to home~~)
text.ru: ***go to** work* · ***go to** school* · ***go to** bed* — без артикля. Но ***go home*** — без **to**! *I go home at five.* (не ~~go to home~~)

text.en: **wake up** = stop sleeping. **get up** = leave your bed. *I wake up at six, but I get up at half past six.*

lessons.subtitle: It's half past seven. At quarter to nine.

text.en: ***What time is it?*** — ***It's** seven **o'clock**.* (7:00). Use **o'clock** only for exact hours. 12:00 in the day = **midday**, at night = **midnight**.
text.ru: ***What time is it?*** — ***It's** seven **o'clock**.* (7:00). **o'clock** — только для ровного часа. 12:00 дня — **midday**, ночи — **midnight**. Перед временем всегда *It's*: ~~Now seven o'clock~~.

text.en: Minutes 1–30: minutes + **past** + this hour. Minutes 31–59: minutes + **to** + the **next** hour.
text.ru: Минуты с 1 по 30: минуты + **past** + текущий час. Минуты с 31 по 59: минуты + **to** + **следующий** час. Сначала минуты, потом час — как в русском «без десяти восемь».

text.en: Careful! **half past seven** is 7:30 — half an hour **after** seven.
text.ru: Осторожно! **half past seven** — это 7:30, полчаса **после** семи. По-русски «половина восьмого» называет следующий час, а по-английски — текущий. *half past seven* = «половина восьмого».

text.en: You can also just say the numbers: *seven thirty* (7:30), *seven forty-five* (7:45), *nine fifteen* (9:15). This is normal for timetables.
text.ru: Можно просто назвать цифры: *seven thirty* (7:30), *seven forty-five* (7:45), *nine fifteen* (9:15). Так обычно говорят о расписаниях.

text.en: English uses the 12-hour clock in speaking: **7 a.m.** = 7:00 in the morning, **7 p.m.** = 19:00. *The shop opens at 9 a.m. and closes at 6 p.m.*
text.ru: В разговоре используют 12-часовой формат: **7 a.m.** — 7:00 утра, **7 p.m.** — 19:00. *The shop opens at 9 a.m. and closes at 6 p.m.* «Девятнадцать часов» по-английски не говорят.

text.en: ***What time** do you get up?* — ***At** seven o'clock.* / ***At** half past six.* **early** = before the usual time, **late** = after it: *I get up early.* *Sorry I'm late!*
text.ru: ***What time** do you get up?* — ***At** seven o'clock.* / ***At** half past six.* **early** — рано, **late** — поздно: *I get up early.* *Sorry I'm late!*

title.en: The present simple: he, she, it and negatives
title.ru: Present simple: he, she, it и отрицания

text.en: With **he, she, it** the verb takes **-s**: *I work → he **works*** · *I live → she **lives*** · *I get up → he **gets** up*.
text.ru: С **he, she, it** к глаголу добавляется **-s**: *I work → he **works*** · *I live → she **lives*** · *I get up → he **gets** up*. Это единственное окончание в настоящем времени — но его забывают чаще всего.

text.en: + **es** after s, sh, ch, x, o: *watch → watch**es**, finish → finish**es**, go → go**es**, do → do**es***. Consonant + y → **ies**: *study → stud**ies***. Irregular: *have → **has***.
text.ru: + **es** после s, sh, ch, x, o: *watch → watch**es**, finish → finish**es**, go → go**es**, do → do**es***. Согласная + y → **ies**: *study → stud**ies***. Неправильный: *have → **has***.

text.en: *I **don't** drive.* *They **don't** work on Sundays.* · *He **doesn't** drive.* *She **doesn't** like coffee.* After **doesn't** the verb has **no -s**: ~~doesn't likes~~.
text.ru: *I **don't** drive.* *They **don't** work on Sundays.* · *He **doesn't** drive.* *She **doesn't** like coffee.* После **doesn't** глагол **без -s**: ~~doesn't likes~~ — окончание уже «ушло» в *does*. И не ~~I not drive~~, ~~he no work~~.

text.en: *I **like** tea.* *She **loves** music.* *He **hates** the gym.* *I **don't like** football.*
text.ru: *I **like** tea.* *She **loves** music.* *He **hates** the gym.* *I **don't like** football.* По-русски «мне нравится чай», а по-английски подлежащее — человек: *I like tea.*

text.en: ***listen to** music* (always **to**) · ***watch** TV* (no article) · ***play** football / tennis* (no article) · ***play the** guitar / piano* (with **the**).
text.ru: ***listen to** music* (всегда с **to**) · ***watch** TV* (без артикля) · ***play** football / tennis* (без артикля) · ***play the** guitar / piano* (с **the**).

h.en: Position: before the verb, after be

text.en: **Before** a normal verb: *I **always get** up early.* *She **never drinks** coffee.* **After** *be*: *I**'m always** tired.* *He **is never** late.*

cafe.title: At the café
cafe.text:
Waiter: Good afternoon. Are you ready to order?
Emma: Yes, please. I'd like a cheese and tomato sandwich, please.
Waiter: Of course. Would you like chips or salad with that?
Emma: Salad, please. I don't want any chips.
Waiter: And for you?
Dan: Have you got any soup today?
Waiter: Yes, we've got tomato soup and chicken soup.
Dan: Can I have the chicken soup, please? And some bread.
Waiter: Certainly. Anything to drink?
Emma: A cup of tea for me, please. With milk, but without sugar.
Dan: And I'd like a glass of orange juice.
Waiter: Would you like anything else? We've got some delicious chocolate cake.
Dan: Oh, yes! Two pieces, please.
Emma: Dan!
(later)
Dan: Excuse me, can we have the bill, please?
Waiter: Here you are. That's eighteen pounds fifty.
Dan: Can I pay by card?
Waiter: Yes, of course.

tr.en: Summary: Emma and Dan are in a café. Emma orders a cheese and tomato sandwich with salad and a cup of tea with milk, without sugar. Dan orders chicken soup with bread, a glass of orange juice and two pieces of chocolate cake. The bill is £18.50 and Dan pays by card.

list.title: The shopping list
list.text:
Sarah: Mark, I'm at the supermarket. What do we need?
Mark: Let me look in the fridge. We've got some milk, but there isn't much. And there aren't any eggs.
Sarah: OK, milk and eggs. How many eggs?
Mark: Twelve, please. I want to make a cake.
Sarah: Have we got any butter?
Mark: Yes, we've got a lot of butter. But we haven't got any sugar.
Sarah: How much sugar do you need?
Mark: A kilo. Oh, and there's no bread.
Sarah: Is there any fruit?
Mark: There are a few apples and one old banana. Can you buy some oranges and a bag of grapes?
Sarah: Of course. Anything else?
Mark: Yes — a big bar of chocolate. For the cake!
Sarah: For the cake… or for you?
Mark: Well… for the cake and for me.

tr.en: Summary: Sarah is at the supermarket and phones Mark. At home there is a little milk, a lot of butter, a few apples and one banana, but no eggs, no sugar and no bread. Mark wants to make a cake. Sarah will buy milk, twelve eggs, a kilo of sugar, bread, oranges, grapes and a big bar of chocolate.

h.en: hungry and thirsty: be, not have
h.ru: hungry и thirsty: be, а не have

text.en: *I**'m** hungry.* (I want to eat.) *I**'m** thirsty.* (I want to drink.) English uses **be** + adjective.
text.ru: *I**'m** hungry.* (Я хочу есть.) *I**'m** thirsty.* (Я хочу пить.) В английском это **be** + прилагательное, а не «хочу есть».

text.en: *I have toast **for** breakfast.* *What do you have **for** lunch?* *We have fish **for** dinner on Fridays.*
text.ru: *I have toast **for** breakfast.* *What do you have **for** lunch?* *We have fish **for** dinner on Fridays.* Русское «на завтрак» — это **for** breakfast.

text.en: British **chips** 🍟 = American *fries*. British **biscuit** 🍪 = American *cookie*. British **crisps** = American *chips*. This course uses British English.
text.ru: Британское **chips** 🍟 = американское *fries*. Британское **biscuit** 🍪 = американское *cookie*. Британское **crisps** (чипсы) = американское *chips*. В курсе — британский вариант.

text.en: *tomato → tomato**es*** · *potato → potato**es*** · *strawberry → strawberr**ies*** · *sandwich → sandwich**es***. **fruit** and **fish** usually have no plural -s: *I eat a lot of fruit.*
text.ru: *tomato → tomato**es*** · *potato → potato**es*** · *strawberry → strawberr**ies*** · *sandwich → sandwich**es***. У **fruit** и **fish** обычно нет -s во множественном числе: *I eat a lot of fruit.*

text.en: When you talk about things in general, use the plural or uncountable **without the**: *I like apple**s**.* *I love chocolate.* *I don't like fish.* (not ~~I like the apples~~)

lessons.subtitle: We've got some milk. There aren't any eggs.

text.en: You can count them: *one egg, two egg**s***. They have **a / an** and a plural: *an apple, three apples, a sandwich*.
text.ru: Их можно посчитать: *one egg, two egg**s***. У них есть **a / an** и множественное число: *an apple, three apples, a sandwich*.

text.en: You can't count them — liquids, materials, masses: *water, milk, bread, rice, sugar, cheese, meat, money*. **No a / an, no plural**: ~~a bread~~, ~~two milks~~, ~~rices~~. The verb is singular: *The milk **is** cold.*
text.ru: Их посчитать нельзя — жидкости, вещества, массы: *water, milk, bread, rice, sugar, cheese, meat, money*. **Без a / an и без множественного числа**: ~~a bread~~, ~~two milks~~, ~~rices~~. Глагол — в единственном числе: *The milk **is** cold.* Осторожно: **bread** и **money** в английском неисчисляемые, хотя по-русски «деньги» — множественное число.

text.en: With plurals and uncountables: **some** in positive sentences, **any** in negatives and questions.
text.ru: Со множественным числом и неисчисляемыми: **some** в утверждениях, **any** в отрицаниях и вопросах.

text.en: Use **some** in questions when you offer or ask for something: *Would you like **some** tea?* *Can I have **some** water?*
text.ru: В вопросах-предложениях и просьбах тоже **some**: *Would you like **some** tea?* *Can I have **some** water?*

h.en: How many + plural, How much + uncountable

text.en: ***How many** eggs do we need?* (countable, plural) · ***How much** milk do we need?* (uncountable).
text.ru: ***How many** eggs do we need?* (исчисляемое, множественное число) · ***How much** milk do we need?* (неисчисляемое). По-русски в обоих случаях «сколько», а в английском нужно выбирать.

text.en: In positive sentences use **a lot of** (or *lots of*) with both types: *I eat **a lot of** fruit.* *She's got **a lot of** friends.* In short answers: *A lot.* (no **of**)
text.ru: В утвердительных предложениях используйте **a lot of** (или *lots of*) с обоими типами: *I eat **a lot of** fruit.* *She's got **a lot of** friends.* В кратком ответе: *A lot.* (без **of**)

h.en: much and many — in negatives and questions
h.ru: much и many — в отрицаниях и вопросах

text.en: *I don't drink **much** coffee.* *There aren't **many** shops here.* *Do you eat **much** meat?* In positive sentences *much* sounds strange: say *a lot of*.
text.ru: *I don't drink **much** coffee.* *There aren't **many** shops here.* *Do you eat **much** meat?* В утверждениях *much* звучит неестественно: говорите *a lot of*. Русское «много» — это три слова: *a lot of, much, many*.

text.en: A small quantity: **a few** + plural (*a few apples*), **a little** + uncountable (*a little milk*).
text.ru: Небольшое количество: **a few** + множественное число (*a few apples*), **a little** + неисчисляемое (*a little milk*).

text.en: **How much** also asks about the price: ***How much is** this cake?* ***How much are** these apples?*
text.ru: **How much** — это ещё и вопрос о цене: ***How much is** this cake?* ***How much are** these apples?*

lessons.subtitle: I'd like a coffee, please. Can I have the bill?

text.en: ***I'd like** a coffee, please.* (= I would like) is polite. *I want a coffee* is too direct for a café. The form is the same for everybody: *I'd like, she'd like, we'd like*.
text.ru: ***I'd like** a coffee, please.* (= I would like) — вежливо. *I want a coffee* в кафе звучит слишком резко. Форма одна для всех лиц: *I'd like, she'd like, we'd like*.

text.en: An offer: ***Would you like** a drink?* — *Yes, please.* / *No, thank you.* · ***What would you like?*** — *I'd like the soup.*
text.ru: Предложение: ***Would you like** a drink?* — *Yes, please.* / *No, thank you.* · ***What would you like?*** — *I'd like the soup.*

text.en: *I **like** coffee.* = always, in general. *I**'d like** a coffee.* = I want one now. *Do you like tea?* (in general) ≠ *Would you like some tea?* (now)
text.ru: *I **like** coffee.* — вообще, всегда. *I**'d like** a coffee.* — хочу сейчас. *Do you like tea?* (вообще) ≠ *Would you like some tea?* (сейчас). Это одна из самых частых ошибок на уровне A1.

text.en: Another polite way to ask: ***Can I have** a glass of water, please?* ***Can we have** the bill, please?* The answer: *Yes, **of course**.* / ***Here you are**.*
text.ru: Ещё один вежливый способ попросить: ***Can I have** a glass of water, please?* ***Can we have** the bill, please?* Ответ: *Yes, **of course**.* / ***Here you are**.* Фразу *Here you are* говорят, когда что-то подают; это не «вот ты где».

text.en: *tea **with** milk* · *coffee **without** sugar* · *a burger **with** chips* · *water **with** ice*.
text.ru: *tea **with** milk* · *coffee **without** sugar* · *a burger **with** chips* · *water **with** ice*.

text.en: In a café, drinks become countable = a cup or glass: ***a coffee**, **two teas**, **an orange juice***.
text.ru: В кафе напитки становятся исчисляемыми — имеется в виду чашка или стакан: ***a coffee**, **two teas**, **an orange juice***.

text.en: *Is that to **eat in** or **take away**?* — *Take away, please.* At the end: *Can I have **the bill**, please?*
text.ru: *Is that to **eat in** or **take away**?* — *Take away, please.* В конце: *Can I have **the bill**, please?* В британских кафе часто заказывают и платят у стойки.

text.en: **£1** = one pound · **£5** = five pound**s** · **50p** = fifty pence (“fifty p”) · **£2.50** = *two pounds fifty* (or *two fifty*) · **£18.99** = *eighteen ninety-nine*. Write the sign **before** the number: £10.

club.title: The weekend club
club.text:
Welcome to the Leeds Weekend Club! We're a group of people who love doing things together in our free time.

On Saturday mornings we go running in the park. You don't need to be fast — we run slowly and we talk a lot! After that we usually have coffee together.

On Saturday afternoons there's a chess club in the library. Can you play chess? It doesn't matter if you can't. Tom can teach you. He's very good at it and he's a great teacher.

On Sundays we often go walking or cycling outside the city. We also go swimming once a month. If it rains, we stay in and play cards or watch a film.

Are you interested in music? Some of us play the guitar and sing. We aren't very good, but it's a lot of fun.

You can join us for one activity or for all of them. It's free, and you can bring your friends. Write to us or call Emma — she can tell you more.

tr.en: Summary: The Leeds Weekend Club is a free group for free-time activities: slow running in the park on Saturday mornings (then coffee), a chess club in the library on Saturday afternoons (Tom teaches beginners), walking or cycling on Sundays, swimming once a month, and cards or a film when it rains. Some members play the guitar and sing. You can come to one activity or all, and bring friends.
tr.ru:
Добро пожаловать в Клуб выходного дня в Лидсе! Мы — компания людей, которые любят проводить свободное время вместе.

В субботу утром мы бегаем в парке. Быстро бегать не нужно — мы бежим медленно и много разговариваем! После этого обычно вместе пьём кофе.

В субботу днём в библиотеке собирается шахматный клуб. Вы умеете играть в шахматы? Если нет — не страшно. Том может вас научить. Он играет очень хорошо и отлично объясняет.

По воскресеньям мы часто ходим в походы или катаемся на велосипедах за городом. Раз в месяц ходим плавать. Если идёт дождь, остаёмся в помещении и играем в карты или смотрим фильм.

Вы интересуетесь музыкой? Некоторые из нас играют на гитаре и поют. Получается не очень, зато весело.

Можно приходить на одно занятие или на все. Это бесплатно, и можно приводить друзей. Напишите нам или позвоните Эмме — она расскажет подробнее.

talk.title: What do you like doing?
talk.text:
Maria: So, Tom, what do you like doing at the weekend?
Tom: I love playing chess. And I like cooking for my friends. What about you?
Maria: I like dancing. I go to a salsa club twice a week.
Tom: Really? I can't dance at all! I'm terrible at it.

way.title: Excuse me, where's the station?
way.text:
Tourist: Excuse me, how do I get to the train station?
Woman: The station? It isn't far. Are you on foot?
Tourist: Yes, I am.
Woman: OK. Go straight on along this street as far as the traffic lights. Then turn left into Bridge Street.
Tourist: Left at the traffic lights.
Woman: Yes. Go over the bridge and past the post office. Then take the second street on the right. That's Station Road.
Tourist: The second on the right…
Woman: Go along Station Road for about two hundred metres. The station is at the end of the road, opposite a big hotel. You can't miss it.
Tourist: How long does it take?
Woman: About ten minutes. Or you can take the number 5 bus from the bus stop over there, but it isn't worth it.
Tourist: No, I'd like to walk. Thank you very much!
Woman: You're welcome. Oh — be careful when you cross Bridge Street. Don't cross at the corner. There's a zebra crossing near the bakery.

tr.en: Summary: A tourist asks a woman the way to the station. Directions: straight on to the traffic lights, turn left into Bridge Street, over the bridge and past the post office, then the second street on the right (Station Road), about 200 metres; the station is at the end, opposite a big hotel. It takes about ten minutes on foot. She also tells him to cross Bridge Street at the zebra crossing near the bakery.

town.title: My town
town.text:
I live in a small town called Ashford. It's about sixty kilometres from London. It takes forty minutes by train.

The town centre is very nice. In the middle of the town there's a big square with a market every Saturday. There's an old church on one side of the square and a library on the other side. The post office is on the corner of the square and High Street. Next to it there's a bakery — they sell delicious bread.

High Street is the main street. There are a lot of shops, two banks, a chemist's and three cafés. At the end of High Street there's a bridge over the river. If you go across the bridge and turn right, you get to the park. I walk through the park every morning on my way to work.

I usually go to work on foot because my office is near my house. It only takes fifteen minutes. But when it rains, I go by bus. The bus stop is opposite my house. I get on there and get off at the third stop.

There isn't a cinema or a shopping centre in Ashford, so at the weekend we often go to London.

tr.en: Summary: The writer lives in Ashford, a small town 60 km from London (40 minutes by train). In the middle is a square with a Saturday market, an old church, a library, the post office on the corner, and a bakery. High Street has shops, banks, a chemist's and cafés; at its end a bridge goes over the river to the park. The writer walks to work (15 minutes) or takes the bus when it rains — three stops. There is no cinema or shopping centre.
tr.ru:
Я живу в маленьком городе под названием Эшфорд. Он примерно в шестидесяти километрах от Лондона. На поезде это сорок минут.

Центр города очень приятный. Посреди города большая площадь, где каждую субботу работает рынок. С одной стороны площади старая церковь, с другой — библиотека. Почта находится на углу площади и Хай-стрит. Рядом с ней пекарня — там продают очень вкусный хлеб.

Хай-стрит — главная улица. Там много магазинов, два банка, аптека и три кафе. В конце Хай-стрит мост через реку. Если перейти мост и повернуть направо, попадёшь в парк. Каждое утро по дороге на работу я иду через парк.

На работу я обычно хожу пешком, потому что офис рядом с домом. Это занимает всего пятнадцать минут. Но когда идёт дождь, я еду на автобусе. Остановка напротив моего дома. Я сажусь там и выхожу на третьей остановке.

В Эшфорде нет ни кинотеатра, ни торгового центра, поэтому в выходные мы часто ездим в Лондон.

lessons.subtitle: Is there a bank near here?

text.en: Ask about a kind of place with **a**: *Excuse me, **is there a** bank **near here**?* — *Yes, there's one on High Street.* / *No, there isn't.* Ask about a special place with **the**: ***Where's the** station?*
text.ru: О типе места спрашивают с **a**: *Excuse me, **is there a** bank **near here**?* — *Yes, there's one on High Street.* / *No, there isn't.* О конкретном месте — с **the**: ***Where's the** station?* Вокзал в городе обычно один, поэтому **the**; банков много — поэтому **a**.

text.en: *Is it **near**?* — *Yes, it's **near here**.* / *It's **near** the station.* · *Is it **far**?* — *No, it isn't **far**.* / *It's **far from** the centre.* **near** has no preposition; **far** needs **from**.
text.ru: *Is it **near**?* — *Yes, it's **near here**.* / *It's **near** the station.* · *Is it **far**?* — *No, it isn't **far**.* / *It's **far from** the centre.* После **near** предлог не нужен; после **far** — **from**.

text.en: ***on** High Street* · ***in** the square* · ***in** the city centre* · ***at** the bus stop* · ***at** the station* · ***on** the corner*.
text.ru: ***on** High Street* (британский вариант: также *in*) · ***in** the square* · ***in** the city centre* · ***at** the bus stop* · ***at** the station* · ***on** the corner*.

text.en: British English often names a shop with **'s**: *the chemist**'s*** (= the chemist's shop), *the baker**'s***, *the butcher**'s***. *I'm going **to the chemist's**.*
text.ru: В британском английском магазин часто называют через **'s**: *the chemist**'s*** (= магазин аптекаря), *the baker**'s***, *the butcher**'s***. *I'm going **to the chemist's**.*

text.en: British **chemist's** = American *pharmacy / drugstore* · **car park** = *parking lot* · **petrol station** = *gas station* · **city centre** = *downtown* · **pavement** = *sidewalk*.
text.ru: Британское **chemist's** = американское *pharmacy / drugstore* · **car park** = *parking lot* · **petrol station** = *gas station* · **city centre** = *downtown* · **pavement** = *sidewalk*.

call.title: A video call
call.text:
Mum: Hello, Emma! Can you hear me? Where are you?
Emma: Hi, Mum! Yes, I can. I'm in Barcelona. I'm sitting in a café near the beach.
Mum: Lucky you! What's the weather like?
Emma: It's wonderful. The sun is shining and it's twenty-six degrees. I'm wearing shorts and a T-shirt!
Mum: It's raining here, of course. And it's freezing. I'm wearing two jumpers. What are you doing?
Emma: I'm having a coffee and waiting for Dan. He's buying postcards.
Mum: Is he enjoying the holiday?
Emma: Yes, he's having a great time. He's learning Spanish! He practises with the waiters every day.
Mum: And are you working? I can see your laptop.
Emma: No, I'm not working! I'm writing to Jack. What's he doing?
Mum: He isn't doing his homework, I know that. He's playing computer games in his room. And your dad is cooking dinner.
Emma: Dad's cooking? He never cooks!
Mum: Well, he's trying. Oh no — something is burning. I have to go!

tr.en: Summary: Emma is on holiday in Barcelona and talks to her mum by video call. She is sitting in a café near the beach in shorts and a T-shirt; it is sunny and 26 degrees. She is having a coffee and waiting for Dan, who is buying postcards and learning Spanish. In Leeds it is raining and freezing; Mum is wearing two jumpers, Jack is playing computer games, and Dad is cooking dinner — and something is burning.
tr.ru:
Мама: Алло, Эмма! Ты меня слышишь? Ты где?
Эмма: Привет, мам! Да, слышу. Я в Барселоне. Сижу в кафе возле пляжа.
Мама: Везёт тебе! Какая там погода?
Эмма: Чудесная. Светит солнце, двадцать шесть градусов. Я в шортах и футболке!
Мама: А у нас, конечно, дождь. И жуткий холод. На мне два свитера. Что ты делаешь?
Эмма: Пью кофе и жду Дэна. Он покупает открытки.
Мама: Ему нравится отпуск?
Эмма: Да, он прекрасно проводит время. Он учит испанский! Каждый день практикуется с официантами.
Мама: А ты работаешь? Я вижу твой ноутбук.
Эмма: Нет, не работаю! Я пишу Джеку. А что он делает?
Мама: Уроки он точно не делает. Играет в компьютерные игры у себя в комнате. А папа готовит ужин.

year.title: The weather where I live
year.text:
I live in Edinburgh, in Scotland. People say the weather here is terrible, but I don't agree. It's just… interesting.

In winter it's cold and dark. It gets dark at four o'clock in the afternoon! It sometimes snows in January and February, but not much. I always wear a warm coat, a scarf and gloves.

Spring starts in March. It's still cool, but the days are longer and there are flowers in the parks. It often rains in April, so I never leave home without an umbrella.

Summer is my favourite season. It isn't hot — usually about eighteen degrees — but in June it's light until eleven o'clock at night. In August there's a big festival and the city is full of people.

In autumn the trees are red and yellow. It's very windy in October and November, and it rains a lot.

Right now it's November. I'm sitting at my window and looking at the street. It's raining, the wind is blowing and people are running for the bus. But I'm drinking hot tea and I'm warm and dry.

tr.en: Summary: The writer lives in Edinburgh. Winter is cold and dark (dark at 4 p.m., a little snow in January and February). Spring starts in March; it often rains in April. Summer is the writer's favourite season: about 18 degrees, light until 11 p.m. in June, a festival in August. Autumn is windy and rainy. Right now it is November: it is raining and windy, but the writer is at home, drinking hot tea.
tr.ru:
Я живу в Эдинбурге, в Шотландии. Говорят, что погода здесь ужасная, но я не согласен. Она просто… интересная.

Зимой холодно и темно. Темнеет в четыре часа дня! В январе и феврале иногда идёт снег, но немного. Я всегда ношу тёплое пальто, шарф и перчатки.

Весна начинается в марте. Ещё прохладно, но дни становятся длиннее, а в парках появляются цветы. В апреле часто идёт дождь, поэтому я никогда не выхожу из дома без зонта.

Лето — моё любимое время года. Здесь не жарко — обычно около восемнадцати градусов, — зато в июне светло до одиннадцати вечера. В августе проходит большой фестиваль, и в городе полно людей.

Осенью деревья красные и жёлтые. В октябре и ноябре очень ветрено и много дождей.

Сейчас ноябрь. Я сижу у окна и смотрю на улицу. Идёт дождь, дует ветер, люди бегут к автобусу. А я пью горячий чай, и мне тепло и сухо.

lessons.subtitle: I'm reading. She's cooking. They're playing.

text.en: For an action happening **now**: **am / is / are** + verb-**ing**. *I**'m reading**.* *She**'s cooking**.* *They**'re playing**.*
text.ru: Для действия, которое происходит **сейчас**: **am / is / are** + глагол с **-ing**. *I**'m reading**.* *She**'s cooking**.* *They**'re playing**.* В русском такого времени нет: «я читаю» — это и *I read* (вообще), и *I'm reading* (прямо сейчас). В английском надо выбирать.

text.en: You need **both** parts: ~~I working~~ ✖️ · ~~I am work~~ ✖️ · *I **am working*** ✔️.

lessons.subtitle: I'm wearing jeans and a jumper.

text.en: ***I'm wearing** jeans **today**.* (now → continuous) · ***I usually wear** a suit to work.* (habit → simple). **wear** = have on your body; **put on** = the action of dressing; **take off** = remove.
text.ru: ***I'm wearing** jeans **today**.* (сейчас → continuous) · ***I usually wear** a suit to work.* (привычка → simple). **wear** — носить, быть одетым; **put on** — надевать (действие); **take off** — снимать. Русское «на мне джинсы» — *I'm wearing jeans*.

text.en: **trousers, jeans, shorts, glasses, sunglasses** are always plural: *My jeans **are** new.* *These trousers **are** too long.* To count: *a **pair of** jeans, two **pairs of** trousers*. Also *a pair of shoes / socks / gloves*.
text.ru: **trousers, jeans, shorts, glasses, sunglasses** — всегда множественное число: *My jeans **are** new.* *These trousers **are** too long.* Считают парами: *a **pair of** jeans, two **pairs of** trousers*. Также *a pair of shoes / socks / gloves*. А **clothes** — тоже только множественное: *My clothes **are** wet.*

lessons.subtitle: It's raining. It's cold and windy.

text.en: English always needs a subject — use **it**: ***It's** sunny.* ***It's** cold.* ***It's** windy.* ***It's** 20 degrees.* ***What's the weather like?*** — *It's warm and sunny.*
text.ru: В английском всегда нужно подлежащее — используйте **it**: ***It's** sunny.* ***It's** cold.* ***It's** windy.* ***It's** 20 degrees.* ***What's the weather like?*** — *It's warm and sunny.* По-русски «холодно», а по-английски обязательно *It's cold*.

text.en: **rain** and **snow** are verbs: ***It's raining**.* (now) · ***It often rains** in April.* (habit) · ***It's snowing**.* · *The sun **is shining**.* · *The wind **is blowing**.*
text.ru: **rain** и **snow** — глаголы: ***It's raining**.* (сейчас) · ***It often rains** in April.* (обычно) · ***It's snowing**.* · *The sun **is shining**.* · *The wind **is blowing**.* Русское «идёт дождь» — не ~~rain goes~~, а *it's raining*.

text.en: *sun → sun**ny*** · *cloud → cloud**y*** · *wind → wind**y*** · *rain → rain**y*** · *snow → snow**y*** · *fog → fog**gy***.
text.ru: *sun → sun**ny*** · *cloud → cloud**y*** · *wind → wind**y*** · *rain → rain**y*** · *snow → snow**y*** · *fog → fog**gy***.

text.en: ***in** January, **in** July* · ***in** (the) spring, **in** summer, **in** autumn, **in** winter* · ***in** 2026*. Months always have a **capital letter**; seasons don't.
text.ru: ***in** January, **in** July* · ***in** (the) spring, **in** summer, **in** autumn, **in** winter* · ***in** 2026*. Месяцы всегда пишутся с **большой буквы**, времена года — с маленькой. Итог по предлогам времени: **at** 7 o'clock · **on** Monday · **in** July / **in** winter / **in** the morning.

text.en: British **autumn** = American *fall*. Temperatures in Britain are in **degrees Celsius**: *It's twenty degrees.* Below zero: *It's **minus five**.*
text.ru: Британское **autumn** = американское *fall*. Температура в Великобритании — в **градусах Цельсия**: *It's twenty degrees.* Ниже нуля: *It's **minus five**.*

title.en: Now or every day? Two present tenses
title.ru: Сейчас или каждый день? Два настоящих времени

lessons.subtitle: I usually walk, but today I'm taking the bus.

text.en: **Present simple** — habits, facts, always true: *I **work** in a bank.* *She **gets up** at seven.* **Present continuous** — happening now or in this period: *I**'m working** at home **today**.* *She**'s getting** up **right now**.*
text.ru: **Present simple** — привычки, факты, то, что верно всегда: *I **work** in a bank.* *She **gets up** at seven.* **Present continuous** — то, что происходит сейчас или в этот период: *I**'m working** at home **today**.* *She**'s getting** up **right now**.* Русское «работаю» — оба варианта; выбирайте по смыслу и по словам-подсказкам.

table: every day · usually · often · never · on Mondays · at the weekend
now · right now · at the moment · today · this week · Look! · Listen!
What do you do? (= your job)

text.en: ***What do you do?*** = What's your job? — *I'm a nurse.* · ***What are you doing?*** = now — *I'm having lunch.*
text.ru: ***What do you do?*** — «Кем вы работаете?» — *I'm a nurse.* · ***What are you doing?*** — «Что вы делаете (сейчас)?» — *I'm having lunch.*

text.en: **have** = possess → simple only: *I **have** a car.* **have** = eat / do → both: *I usually **have** lunch at one.* / *I**'m having** lunch now.*

weekend.title: A terrible Saturday
weekend.text:
Last Saturday was the worst day of my year.

I wanted to go to London for my friend Anna's birthday party. I woke up late because I forgot to set my alarm. I didn't have time for breakfast. I ran to the station, but I missed my train by one minute!

The next train was an hour later. I bought a coffee and sat on the platform. It was cold and it started to rain. Then I looked in my bag for Anna's present — and it wasn't there. It was at home, on the kitchen table.

I finally arrived in London at two o'clock. I took the underground, but I got on the wrong train and went north, not south. I lost another forty minutes.

When I got to Anna's flat, the door was closed and nobody answered. I called her. “Where are you?” she asked. “At your flat!” I said. She laughed. “Tom, the party is next Saturday!”

In the end we went to a café and had a wonderful afternoon. And the next week I didn't forget the present.

tr.en: Summary: Tom wanted to go to London for Anna's birthday party. He woke up late, had no breakfast and missed his train by one minute. He waited an hour in the rain and then saw that the present was at home. In London he took the wrong underground train and lost forty minutes. At Anna's flat nobody answered: the party was next Saturday. In the end they went to a café and had a wonderful afternoon.
tr.ru:
Прошлая суббота была худшим днём моего года.

Я хотел поехать в Лондон на день рождения подруги Анны. Проснулся поздно, потому что забыл поставить будильник. На завтрак времени не было. Я побежал на вокзал, но опоздал на поезд на одну минуту!

Следующий поезд был через час. Я купил кофе и сел на платформе. Было холодно, и начался дождь. Потом я полез в сумку за подарком для Анны — а его там не было. Он остался дома, на кухонном столе.

В Лондон я наконец приехал в два часа. Сел в метро, но перепутал поезд и поехал на север, а не на юг. Потерял ещё сорок минут.

Когда я добрался до квартиры Анны, дверь была закрыта, и никто не ответил. Я позвонил ей. «Ты где?» — спросила она. «У твоей квартиры!» — сказал я. Она засмеялась. «Том, вечеринка в следующую субботу!»

В итоге мы пошли в кафе и чудесно провели день. А через неделю я подарок не забыл.

life.title: My grandmother
life.text:
My grandmother's name was Helen. She was born in 1935 in a small village in Scotland. Her family wasn't rich. There were six children, and they all lived in a house with two bedrooms.

She left school when she was fourteen and started work in a shop. She didn't like it, but she needed the money. In the evenings she studied, because she wanted to be a nurse.

In 1955 she moved to Edinburgh and got a job at a hospital. She met my grandfather there. He was a patient — he had a broken leg! They got married in 1958 and had three children.

My grandmother worked as a nurse for forty years. She never drove a car and she never flew in a plane. But she read hundreds of books and she could speak French, because she learned it from the radio.

When I was a child, I stayed with her every summer. She made wonderful cakes and told me stories about the past. She died ten years ago, and I still think about her every day.

tr.en: Summary: The writer's grandmother Helen was born in 1935 in a village in Scotland, in a poor family with six children. She left school at fourteen, worked in a shop and studied in the evenings to be a nurse. In 1955 she moved to Edinburgh, worked at a hospital and met the writer's grandfather, a patient with a broken leg; they married in 1958 and had three children. She was a nurse for forty years, never drove or flew, read a lot and learned French from the radio. She died ten years ago.
tr.ru:
Мою бабушку звали Хелен. Она родилась в 1935 году в маленькой деревне в Шотландии. Её семья была небогатой. Детей было шестеро, и все они жили в доме с двумя спальнями.

Она ушла из школы в четырнадцать лет и начала работать в магазине. Ей это не нравилось, но нужны были деньги. По вечерам она училась, потому что хотела стать медсестрой.

В 1955 году она переехала в Эдинбург и устроилась в больницу. Там она встретила моего дедушку. Он был пациентом — со сломанной ногой! Они поженились в 1958 году, и у них родилось трое детей.

Бабушка проработала медсестрой сорок лет. Она никогда не водила машину и никогда не летала на самолёте. Зато прочитала сотни книг и говорила по-французски, потому что выучила его по радио.

В детстве я каждое лето гостил у неё. Она пекла чудесные пироги и рассказывала мне истории о прошлом. Она умерла десять лет назад, а я до сих пор думаю о ней каждый день.

text.en: For finished actions in the past: *I work**ed**.* *She work**ed**.* *They work**ed**.* No -s, no change — the same form for all persons.
text.ru: Для завершённых действий в прошлом: *I work**ed**.* *She work**ed**.* *They work**ed**.* Без -s, без изменений — одна форма для всех лиц. В русском глагол меняется по родам и числам (работал, работала, работали), а в английском — нет.

text.en: + **ed**: *watch → watch**ed***. After **e**, only + **d**: *live → live**d**, like → like**d***. Consonant + **y** → **ied**: *study → stud**ied**, try → tr**ied*** (but *play → play**ed***). Short vowel + consonant → double it: *stop → stop**ped***. British English: *travel → trave**lled***.
text.ru: + **ed**: *watch → watch**ed***. После **e** — только + **d**: *live → live**d**, like → like**d***. text.en: Negative: **didn't** + the **base** verb (no -ed, no irregular form): *I **didn't go**.* *She **didn't like** it.* *We **didn't see** him.* Not ~~didn't went~~, ~~didn't liked~~.

plans.title: Next year
plans.text:
Emma: Dan, it's almost the end of the year. What are your plans for next year?
Dan: Well, first, I'm going to change jobs. I don't like my office. It's too far from home and my boss is the worst manager in the company.
Emma: Really? What are you going to do?
Dan: I'm going to look for a job in a smaller company. Smaller companies are friendlier, I think. And I'd like to work nearer home.
Emma: Good idea. I'm going to finish my course in June. Then I'm going to take the exam.
Dan: Are you going to pass?
Emma: I hope so! I'm going to study every evening. It's the most difficult exam of the course.
Dan: And what about the summer? Are we going to go to Barcelona again?
Emma: I'd like to go to a different place this time. What about Scotland? It's cheaper than Spain, and it's more beautiful.
Dan: But it's colder! And it's going to rain every day.
Emma: Maybe. But the mountains are wonderful. And my grandmother's village is there.
Dan: OK, Scotland in July. But I'm going to take a very warm jumper.

tr.en: Summary: Emma and Dan talk about next year. Dan is going to change jobs: his office is too far and his boss is the worst manager; he wants a smaller, friendlier company nearer home. Emma is going to finish her course in June, study every evening and take the most difficult exam. For the summer Emma suggests Scotland — cheaper and more beautiful than Spain; Dan says it is colder and rainy, but agrees: Scotland in July, with a warm jumper.

cities.title: Three cities
cities.text:
People often ask me: which is the best city in the UK? I lived in three of them, so here is my answer.

London is the biggest and the most famous. About nine million people live there. It's also the most expensive: a small flat costs more than a big house in the north. London is noisier and busier than other cities, but it's the most interesting place for museums, theatres and food from all over the world.

Manchester is smaller and cheaper than London. It's the best city for music and football. The people are friendlier, I think, and life is slower. But the weather is worse — it rains more than in London.

Edinburgh is the smallest of the three, and for me it's the most beautiful. It's older and quieter than Manchester, with a castle in the middle of the city. It's colder than London, and in winter the days are much shorter. But in summer it's as busy as London, because of the festival.

So which is the best? In my opinion, London is the best for a weekend, Manchester is the best for a night out, and Edinburgh is the best for life.

tr.en: Summary: The writer compares three UK cities. London is the biggest, most famous, most expensive, noisier and busier, but the most interesting. Manchester is smaller and cheaper, best for music and football, friendlier and slower, but with worse weather. Edinburgh is the smallest and the most beautiful, older, quieter and colder, with short winter days, but as busy as London in summer. tr.ru:
Меня часто спрашивают: какой город в Великобритании самый лучший? Я жил в трёх, так что вот мой ответ.

Лондон — самый большой и самый знаменитый. Там живёт около девяти миллионов человек. Он же и самый дорогой: маленькая квартира стоит больше, чем большой дом на севере. Лондон шумнее и суетливее других городов, зато это самое интересное место: музеи, театры и еда со всего мира.

Манчестер меньше и дешевле Лондона. Это лучший город для музыки и футбола. Люди там, по-моему, дружелюбнее, а жизнь спокойнее. Но погода хуже — дождей больше, чем в Лондоне.

Эдинбург — самый маленький из трёх и, на мой взгляд, самый красивый. Он старше и тише Манчестера, с замком посреди города. Там холоднее, чем в Лондоне, а зимой дни гораздо короче. Зато летом там так же многолюдно, как в Лондоне, — из-за фестиваля.

Так какой же лучший? По-моему, Лондон лучше всего подходит для выходных, Манчестер — для вечера с друзьями, а Эдинбург — для жизни.

h.en: Four ways to talk about time

text.en: You can now talk about every day, now, the past and the future.
text.ru: Теперь вы можете говорить о привычках, о настоящем моменте, о прошлом и о будущем.

table: I **work** in a bank. She **works**. Do you work? I don't work.
I**'m working**. She**'s working**. Are you working? I'm not working.
I **worked**. I **went**. Did you go? I didn't go.
I**'m going to work**. Are you going to work?

text.en: *I **am**, you **are**, she **is*** → past: *I **was**, you **were*** · *I**'ve got** a car. She**'s got** two brothers.* → past: *I **had** a car.*
text.ru: *I **am**, you **are**, she **is*** → прошедшее: *I **was**, you **were*** · *I**'ve got** a car. She**'s got** two brothers.* → прошедшее: *I **had** a car.*

text.en: **a / an** (one, new) · **the** (we know which) · **some / any** · **this / that / these / those** · **my, your, his, her, our, their** · **me, him, her, us, them** · **there is / there are**.
text.ru: **a / an** (один, новый) · **the** (понятно какой) · **some / any** · **this / that / these / those** · **my, your, his, her, our, their** · **me, him, her, us, them** · **there is / there are**.

text.en: **Time:** *at* seven · *on* Monday · *in* July / *in* the morning. **Place:** *in* the kitchen · *on* the table · *at* home / *at* work · *next to, under, between, opposite*. **Movement:** *to* the station · *into* the shop · *along* the street · *across* the road.
text.ru: **Время:** *at* seven · *on* Monday · *in* July / *in* the morning. **Место:** *in* the kitchen · *on* the table · *at* home / *at* work · *next to, under, between, opposite*. **Движение:** *to* the station · *into* the shop · *along* the street · *across* the road.

h.en: The most common mistakes of Russian speakers

text.en: 1. No verb: ~~She doctor~~ → *She **is a** doctor.* 2. No article: ~~I have car~~ → *I have **a** car.* 3. No -s: ~~He work~~ → *He work**s**.* 4. No *do*: ~~You like tea?~~ → ***Do** you like tea?* 5. Double past: ~~didn't went~~ → *didn't **go**.* 6. ~~I am agree~~ → *I agree.* 7. ~~more cheaper~~ → *cheaper*.
text.ru: 1. Нет глагола: ~~She doctor~~ → *She **is a** doctor.* 2. Нет артикля: ~~I have car~~ → *I have **a** car.* 3. Нет -s: ~~He work~~ → *He work**s**.* 4. Нет *do*: ~~You like tea?~~ → ***Do** you like tea?* 5. Двойное прошедшее: ~~didn't went~~ → *didn't **go**.* 6. ~~I am agree~~ → *I agree.* 7. ~~more cheaper~~ → *cheaper*.

text.en: **Practise** a little every day. Don't be afraid of **mistakes** — they are part of your **progress**. Read, listen and speak as much as you can.
text.ru: **Practise** — понемногу каждый день. Не бойтесь **ошибок** — они часть вашего **прогресса**. Читайте, слушайте и говорите как можно больше.

text.en: At A2 you will learn the present perfect (*I have been to London*), *will* for the future, *should* and *must*, longer stories in the past (*I was walking when…*), and a lot more vocabulary for travel, work and health.

Hi Sam!

My name's Anna and I'm from Russia. I'm twenty-eight and I work as an analyst in a bank. I've got one brother. His name's Pavel and he's older than me. I live in a small flat in Kazan. There are two rooms and a balcony. Kazan is smaller than Moscow, but in my opinion it's more beautiful. I usually get up at seven and go to work by bus. In my free time I like reading and cooking. Last weekend I went to the theatre with my friends. It was wonderful! Next year I'm going to travel to Scotland. What about you? Where do you live? What do you like doing?

Write soon!
Anna
